what_its_for: Omacetaxine is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of blood cancer called chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). It is used when other cancer medicines, such as imatinib or dasatinib, have stopped working or cannot be tolerated. It works by slowing or stopping the growth of cancer cells in your body.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection under your skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your upper arm, thigh, or belly area. A healthcare provider will give you this injection, or you may be trained to give it to yourself at home. Never inject it into a vein or muscle. Rotate injection sites each time to avoid skin irritation. Do not shake the vial. Use a new needle and syringe for each injection and dispose of sharps safely in an approved sharps container.
dosing: The dose your doctor prescribes depends on your treatment phase and your body surface area. For the induction phase, the typical dose is 1.25 mg per square meter of body surface area, injected twice daily for 14 days in a row, followed by a 14-day rest period (making a 28-day cycle). For the maintenance phase, the same dose is given twice daily for 7 days, followed by a 21-day rest period. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on your blood counts and how well you tolerate the medicine.
missed_dose: If you miss a scheduled injection, contact your doctor or healthcare team right away for guidance. Do not try to make up a missed dose on your own or take a double dose. Your doctor will advise you on the best next step based on your treatment schedule.
storage: Store unopened vials of omacetaxine in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep vials in the original packaging to protect them from light. Once the solution has been prepared or mixed, it may be stored at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) or in the refrigerator for up to 12 hours. Discard any unused portion after 12 hours. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze.
what_to_avoid: Avoid activities that increase your risk of bleeding or injury, such as contact sports, because this medicine can lower your platelet count and make it harder for your blood to clot. Avoid crowded places and contact with people who are sick, as this medicine can weaken your immune system and make you more likely to get infections. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Both men and women should use effective birth control during treatment and for a period after stopping. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay. Talk to your doctor before taking any new medicines, vitamins, or supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: unusual bleeding or bruising (such as nosebleeds, bleeding gums, blood in your urine or stools, or cuts that will not stop bleeding); signs of infection such as fever (temperature above 100.4°F / 38°C), chills, cough, or burning with urination; severe tiredness or dizziness; confusion or changes in vision; chest pain or shortness of breath; signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision, or fruity-smelling breath; severe skin reactions at the injection site such as increasing redness, swelling, pain, or oozing; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Omacetaxine does not work overnight. It may take several weeks to months of treatment before your doctor can measure how well it is working through blood tests and bone marrow tests. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own even if you feel well or do not notice changes. Your doctor will monitor your progress regularly with lab tests to check your blood counts and response to treatment.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: This medicine can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Elderly Patients: Older patients (65 years and above) may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially low blood counts and fatigue. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or Liver Problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or you may need extra monitoring. Diabetes: This medicine can raise your blood sugar levels. Tell your doctor if you have diabetes or are at risk for it, as you may need closer blood sugar monitoring.
